Testing Strategy & Frameworks 2.1 Scope of Testing Elements 2.1.1 Target Functional Areas (In-Scope) Identity Isolation: Verification of multi-factor user login challenges and secure token generation loops. Pipeline Integrity: Parsing mechanics handling edge cases, boundary parameters, and structural validation routines. Data Preservation: Verifying that data mutations are written accurately to persistent relational tables during stress conditions. 2.1.2 Excluded Elements (Out-of-Scope) Cross-Browser Legacy Checking: Verification is restricted to modern browser layouts and will skip deprecated engines. Third-Party Network Invalidation: Testing stops at integration gateways; stability verification of external dependency servers is excluded. 2.2 Testing Levels & Methodologies The team utilizes a bottom-up validation methodology to guarantee that individual code components pass verification metrics before system integration. [ Unit Testing (Jest) ] ➔ [ Integration Verification ] ➔ [ End-to-End Workflows ] 2.2.1 Unit Testing Strategy Individual utility functions, controllers, and schema validators are isolated using mock frameworks. This keeps unit routines independent of network adapters or active database instances. 2.2.2 Integration & System Verification Strategy Decoupled modules are tested as a unified runtime environment. API routing structures are checked against live database containers to find relational or data mapping bugs early. 3. Test Environment & Tooling Infrastructure 3.1 Environment Hardware Configuration Local Simulation Node: Development workstation provisioned with 8 CPU Cores, 16GB RAM, running an isolated Docker Desktop subsystem. CI Build Staging Server: Automated cloud instance provisioned with 2 Virtual CPUs and 4GB Memory limits to run regression validation sweeps. 3.2 Software Testing Stack Unit & Assertion Engine: Jest / PyTest framework tools. Interface Automation: Playwright / Cypress for end-to-end user path simulation. Load Stress Simulation: k6 / Apache JMeter for performance bottleneck discovery. 4. Detailed Non-Functional Test Cases 5.1 Performance & Latency Metrics (TST-PER) 5.1.1 Test Case: TST-PER-01 — Query Latency Verification Under Baseline Volume Objective: Verify API layer processing limits run within acceptable durations under target operational volumes. Methodology: Execute k6 script scaling up to 500 virtual users calling search endpoints concurrently for 10 minutes. Success Metric: P95 response durations must remain under 200 milliseconds with a zero-error rate response profile. 5.2 Recovery & Resilience Verification (TST-RES) 5.2.1 Test Case: TST-RES-02 — Primary Relational Node Disconnection Failover Objective: Validate storage resilience paths when database runtime failures occur. Methodology: Force-terminate the primary database container while active client pipelines are writing transaction entries. Success Metric: System switches to replica cache within 30 seconds; data mutations roll back cleanly to avoid state corruption. 6. Action Required: Stops the build cycle; requires an immediate solution before any other tasks can advance. 6.2.2 Major Severity Condition: Core functional path fails to process parameters, but an alternative operational workflow exists. Action Required: Must be resolved before entering the formal milestone submission workflow. 6.2.3 Minor Severity Condition: Interface anomalies, cosmetic styling misalignments, or minor logging syntax defects. Action Required: Addressed during standard sprint clean-up cycles as schedule permits.
